note.explanation: A system is the part of a change that we are studying. Everything outside it is the surrounding. Energy moving into the system makes the change endothermic; energy moving out makes it exothermic.
note.checkAnswer: The water is the system. Heat energy moves from the burner and surroundings into the water, so boiling is endothermic.
note.simple: Think of the system as the main thing being studied. The surrounding is everything around it. Follow the energy: going in means endothermic; going out means exothermic.
note.checkQuestion: If energy moves from a system to its surrounding, is the change endothermic or exothermic?
note.title: System and Surrounding
steps: Identify the part of the change being studied: that is the system.
Identify everything outside the system: that is the surrounding.
Check the direction of energy transfer.
Energy entering the system means endothermic and has a positive sign.
Energy leaving the system means exothermic and has a negative sign.
note.answer: Energy moves from the system to the surrounding: the change is exothermic and has a negative sign.

mcqs.stem: When water is heated in a beaker and the water is being studied, what is the system?
rationales: The burner is outside the water being studied, so it is part of the surrounding.
The water is the part being studied, so it is the system.
The room air is outside the system, so it is part of the surrounding.
The beaker is around the water and is part of the surrounding in this example.

options: Energy moves from the system to the surrounding.
Energy moves from the surrounding to the system.
mcqs.stem: Which energy transfer describes an endothermic change?
rationales: Energy leaving the system describes an exothermic change.
Energy entering the system from the surrounding describes an endothermic change.
The definition depends on energy transfer into the system, not on there being no transfer.
Energy transfer does not change which part has been defined as the system.

mcqs.stem: What sign is given to an endothermic change in this section?
rationales: An endothermic change transfers energy into the system and has a positive sign.
A negative sign is associated with an exothermic change.
Zero is not the sign given for an endothermic change.
The section states that endothermic changes have a positive sign.

options: The sign depends only on the container
mcqs.stem: A reaction transfers energy from its system to the surrounding. What sign does the change carry?
rationales: A positive sign is associated with energy transferred into the system.
Energy transferred from the system to the surrounding is exothermic and carries a negative sign.
The section does not assign zero to this energy transfer.
The sign is determined by the direction of energy transfer, not just by the container.

mcqs.stem: In a chemical reaction, what is everything that does not belong to the system called?
rationales: The system is the change or reaction being studied, not everything outside it.
Everything outside the system is called the surrounding.
A catalyst may be included in the system when it is important to study the reaction.
Energy transfer describes movement of energy; it is not the name for everything outside the system.

mcqs.stem: During an exothermic change, what happens to the surrounding as it receives energy from the system?
rationales: The surrounding receives energy from the system and gets warmer.
The section's figure shows the surrounding gets cooler when energy enters the system, not when it receives energy.
An exothermic change does not mean that the system disappears.
Energy is transferred from the system to the surrounding in an exothermic change.

written.text: Does boiling water in a beaker endothermic or exothermic change? Which form of energy is being transferred in this system.
written.finalAnswer: Boiling water is an endothermic change. Heat energy is transferred from the surrounding to the water (the system).

explain.title: The system
explain.body: In Chemistry, any physical or chemical change under study may also be called a system. The chemical reaction includes reactants, products, catalyst, solvent and anything else which is important to study this reaction.

explain.title: The surrounding
explain.body: Everything else which does not fall in this system is called the surrounding. For boiling water in a beaker, the water molecules are the system, while the beaker and burner are part of the surrounding.

explain.title: Energy entering the system
explain.body: When energy is transferred from surrounding to the system, the change is called endothermic and it has a positive sign. The surroundings get cooler as they give energy to the system.

explain.title: Energy leaving the system
explain.body: When energy is transferred from system to surrounding, the change is called exothermic and it carries a negative sign. The surroundings get warmer as they receive energy.

mistakes: Do not call everything in the beaker the system automatically; identify the part being studied. In the boiling-water example, the water is the system.
Do not reverse the direction: energy entering the system is endothermic, while energy leaving it is exothermic.
Do not mix up the signs: endothermic is positive and exothermic is negative.
Name the energy form as heat or thermal energy when asked which form is transferred.
